parties.respondent: The Director General, Border Security Force & Ors.

summary: The appellant, a BSF constable, was convicted by a General Security Force Court for murder under Section 46 of the BSF Act, read with Section 302 IPC, based on firing that caused death of a civilian. The conviction was upheld by the High Court. The appellant claimed private defence, citing hostile border conditions and prior attacks on BSF personnel. The Supreme Court examined the applicability of private defence under Sections 96–106 IPC, emphasizing preponderance of probability standard and reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt. Reliance was placed on medical and eyewitness testimony, including PW-10's forensic evidence and conflicting accounts on whether the deceased was kneeling. The Court evaluated whether the right to private defence extended to causing death under Section 100 IPC.
legal_provisions_cited: Rizan and Another v. State of Chhattisgarh, (2003) 2 SCC 661
State of M.P. v. Ramesh, (2005) 9 SCC 705
final_judgment: Appeal allowed; conviction set aside; appellant acquitted
